objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with epigastric discomfort and cramping pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve had epigastric discomfort with cramping pain for the past two hours, and this has happened before—usually after I eat. I’ve also lost some weight because I’ve been avoiding meals to lessen the pain.
Does the pain radiate to your back, right shoulder, or chest?
Patient: It doesn’t really radiate to my back, right shoulder, or into my chest. It feels mostly centered in the upper middle of my abdomen and cramps there, especially after I eat.
Have you been experiencing nausea or vomiting, and if so, does the pain improve after you vomit?
Patient: No, I haven’t had nausea or vomiting, and the pain doesn’t change because of that. It mostly stays centered in my upper abdomen and tends to be worse after I eat.
Do you feel full unusually quickly when you eat, or does the pain come on after you've finished a normal-sized meal?

Patient: I feel like the pain starts after I eat and gets worse as the meal sits, so I end up eating less because a normal portion triggers it. I don’t usually feel uncomfortably full right away, but I can’t tolerate meals for long after they start.
Have you noticed any black, tarry stools or vomiting of blood or coffee-ground material?

Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any black tarry stools, and I haven’t vomited blood or anything that looks like coffee grounds. I just get the upper middle abdominal cramping that’s worse after I eat, and that’s why I’ve been avoiding meals.
Do you take aspirin, ibuprofen, or other anti-inflammatory medications regularly, or do you have a history of heart disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, or smoking?

I don’t take anything regularly for this, but I do use over-the-counter painkillers for my knee pain. I don’t have heart disease or high blood pressure, but I do smoke and I drink alcohol only occasionally.
What specific over-the-counter painkillers do you take for your knee pain—are they ibuprofen, naproxen, aspirin, or acetaminophen (Tylenol), and how often do you take them?

Patient: I usually take ibuprofen over the counter for my knee pain, about a couple of times a week when it flares, and I don’t take it daily. I’m not taking aspirin regularly, and I mostly avoid naproxen.
How old are you?
I’m 38 years old.
How long has this pattern of post-meal pain been going on—days, weeks, or months?
Patient: It’s been going on for months, with episodes that usually flare after I eat and then improve if I avoid meals, which is why I’ve lost some weight.
Does the pain ever wake you up at night when your stomach is empty, or does it only occur after you eat?
Patient: It mostly only happens after I eat, and I haven’t noticed it waking me up at night when I’m empty. It tends to start once I’ve eaten and cramps get worse as I keep eating or the meal sits.
Do you notice if the pain is triggered specifically by fatty or greasy foods, or does it occur with any type of meal?
Patient: It seems to happen with most meals, not only fatty or greasy foods, and it consistently gets worse as I keep eating or as the meal sits.
Do you ever feel bloated or notice your abdomen getting visibly distended after meals, or have you vomited undigested food hours after eating?
Patient: I do feel some bloating after I eat, but I haven’t noticed major visible distension or swelling of my abdomen. I also haven’t vomited undigested food hours after meals.
Do you have any difficulty swallowing, or a sensation that food gets stuck when you eat?

Patient: No, I don’t have any trouble swallowing, and I don’t feel like food gets stuck when I eat. It’s mainly the cramping upper middle abdominal pain that starts after I eat and gets worse the longer I keep eating.
Have you ever been tested for H. pylori, had a previous ulcer diagnosis, or do you have a family history of stomach cancer or celiac disease?
Patient: I haven’t been tested for H. pylori, and I’ve never been told I have an ulcer. I’m not aware of any family history of stomach cancer or celiac disease.
